To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

i) the optimal detection performance is achieved at the asymptote of the low energy regime and ii) the presence of a physical layer attacker does not significantly degrade the achievable detection performances, with respect the absence of countermeasure.

1) the secrecy requirement does not affect the optimal detection performance in the asymptote; 2) in the low energy regime, the optimal detection performances under secrecy are the same as those achievable without countermeasures; 3) the optimal detection performances are achieved at the same operative point as in the absence of secrecy constraints; 4) in both cases, the optimal operative point is located at the asymptote of the low energy regime.

(i) the network can achieve perfect secrecy at physical layer, (ii) the optimal detection performance is achieved by using a very small amount of energy, and (iii) the secrecy constraint has a negligible impact on the detection performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a novel class of distributed detection systems, in which the sensors implement censoring strategies to save energy and the network is attacked by an eavesdropping adversary.
the design of a distributed binary detection system that implements a censoring strategy and that is resilient against an eavesdropping attack.

the design of distributed detection systems that can operate under severe energy constraints, in the presence of a malicious eavesdropper, and with the characterization of their detection performances.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the secrecy requirement does not impact significantly on the performances of the system.
perfect secrecy can be achieved with no significant loss in terms of detection performances, even in the presence of energy constraints.
, under physical layer secrecy, the detection performances are degraded, but the system can operate at a lower energy level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the perfect secrecy requirement does not significantly impact on the achievable performances of the system.
physical layer secrecy is a very expensive requirement in the context of distributed detection.
, in the presence of a powerful eavesdropper, the optimal solution for the network is to work with low energy levels and low detection rates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the secrecy requirement can be satisfied at a negligible cost in terms of detection performances, even when the eavesdropping capability of the attacker is very high.
physical layer secrecy does not imply a performance degradation of the system.
physical layer secrecy is a viable option in the context of distributed detection with censoring sensors, and that the secrecy constraint has a negligible impact on the performances of the system.
